title: auth: unify auth header semantics + request-signature nonce header + CORS updates for OpenAI-compat
author: Priya Raman
description: Motivation: We have a number of inconsistencies between the Redwood native auth headers and the OpenAI compatibility layer (different header names, incomplete CORS exposure, and no first-class support for signed request nonces). This PR unifies header semantics across the API surface, introduces an opt-in request nonce header for request signing (to reduce replay attack surface for signed tokens), and fixes CORS exposure so browser clients using OpenAI-compat behave the same as native clients. Summary of changes: consolidate supported auth header names, add X-Redwood-Request-Nonce (and accept X-OpenAI-Request-Nonce for compat), ensure Access-Control-Expose-Headers includes the new headers, add scoped token parsing for project/org keys, add behavioral tests, and update docs + migration notes. Checklist: - [x] Spec and implementation for header semantics - [x] Backwards-compatible OpenAI-compat mapping (Authorization / x-api-key) - [x] New nonce header support behind feature flag DEFAULT_ENABLE_REQUEST_NONCE - [x] CORS preflight exposure and allow-headers update - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Docs update and migration notes Rollout plan: feature is behind env feature flag DEFAULT_ENABLE_REQUEST_NONCE (false in prod by default). We will enable in staging for 48 hours, run compatibility test suites with major customers, then enable in canary rollout for 5% traffic before full rollout. Deprecation: old custom header "X-Redwood-Auth" will be supported for 3 months and emit a telemetry counter; docs include migration instructions. Compatibility notes: OpenAI-compat routes will accept both traditional OpenAI Authorization: Bearer <token> and Redwood project/org key forms (proj_ / org_ prefixes), and scoped tokens (scoped:read:model) are parsed consistently. For signed requests we accept a new nonce header (X-Redwood-Request-Nonce) and the compatibility alias X-OpenAI-Request-Nonce. The nonce is validated for uniqueness within a 5 minute window (configurable). Nonce validation is no-op unless request-signing feature is enabled for the tenant.

release_notes: - Unify auth header parsing: support proj_/org_ prefixes consistently across native and OpenAI-compat routes. - Add X-Redwood-Request-Nonce (and X-OpenAI-Request-Nonce alias) to opt-in request signing flow (feature-flagged). - CORS: expose auth and nonce headers to browsers so OpenAI-compat clients can access response headers. - Deprecate legacy X-Redwood-Auth header (3 month support window).
